ansible-lint-issue.remediation: Follow the native ansible-lint rule documentation identified by native_rule_id and help_url.

become-scope-too-broad.description: become: true is applied at play level, granting all tasks root access.
become-scope-too-broad.remediation: Move become: true to the specific tasks that require privilege escalation; use become_user for fine-grained control.

broken-role-dependency.description: A local role dependency is missing, cyclic, or self-referential.
broken-role-dependency.remediation: Correct the local role name, remove self/cyclic edges, or declare the external dependency explicitly.

commit-message-format.description: The latest commit message violates the review format.
commit-message-format.remediation: Rewrite the commit message to satisfy the configured subject/body length and separation policy.

complex-expression.description: A Jinja or conditional expression is excessively complex.
complex-expression.remediation: Extract intermediate variables or split the condition into named, independently understandable checks.

complex-playbook.remediation: Separate unrelated responsibilities and reduce deeply connected imports, roles, or task groups.

credentials-leaking-in-log.description: A task handles a sensitive value without no_log: true.
credentials-leaking-in-log.remediation: Set effective no_log: true on the sensitive task or block and avoid printing the sensitive result.

default-credentials.description: A credential uses a well-known default value.
default-credentials.remediation: Replace the default credential, rotate it if deployed, and retrieve the replacement from a protected source.

deprecated-module-option.description: A task uses a deprecated Ansible module option.
deprecated-module-option.remediation: Replace or remove the option using the reported collection metadata and test against the target version.

deprecated-modules.description: A deprecated Ansible module is in use and may break in future versions.
deprecated-modules.remediation: Replace the deprecated module with the reported supported module/FQCN and test behavior on the target Ansible version.

duplicate-task-names.description: Multiple tasks share the same name.
duplicate-task-names.remediation: Give each task a name that distinguishes its purpose or target.

duplicated-code.remediation: Extract the repeated task body into an included task file or role when the duplication is intentional reuse.

empty-abstraction.description: A task file or nested task abstraction is empty.
empty-abstraction.remediation: Remove the empty file/block or add the intended tasks before enabling it.

excessive-nesting.description: Nested block/rescue/always structures exceed the depth threshold.
excessive-nesting.remediation: Extract nested blocks into named task files or roles and simplify shared conditions/error handling.

fqcn-migration.description: A task uses a short module name instead of the fully-qualified collection name.
fqcn-migration.remediation: Use the fully-qualified collection name (FQCN) such as 'ansible.builtin.copy' instead of the legacy short form.

galaxy-meta-incomplete.description: Optional Galaxy-publication policy: a role's meta/main.yml is missing galaxy_info fields.
galaxy-meta-incomplete.remediation: Populate the required galaxy_info fields (author, description, min_ansible_version) in meta/main.yml.

hardcoded-credentials.description: A hardcoded secret was detected by GitLeaks.
hardcoded-credentials.remediation: Remove the literal secret, rotate it if live, and load it from Ansible Vault or an approved secret manager.

high-coupling.remediation: Review whether imports and roles can be grouped behind a smaller, cohesive role interface.

incohesive-play.description: A play's tasks span multiple unrelated module domains (high module-domain entropy).
incohesive-play.remediation: Group related tasks together or split unrelated responsibilities after manually checking the semantic signal.

incohesive-playbook.description: A playbook's tasks span multiple unrelated module domains (high module-domain entropy).
incohesive-playbook.remediation: Review whether unrelated responsibilities should move into separate playbooks or roles.

incomplete-task.description: An unresolved TODO/FIXME marker remains in configuration code.
incomplete-task.remediation: Complete the marked work, link it to tracked work, or remove the stale marker.

inconsistent-naming-convention.description: A task or play name has excessive special characters.
inconsistent-naming-convention.remediation: Use the project's agreed task/play naming style and avoid decorative punctuation.

insecure-permissions.description: A managed resource grants unsafe permissions to other users.
insecure-permissions.remediation: Use the least-permissive mode required and protect private or sensitive material from group/other access.

insufficient-modularization.description: Playbook is large with many plays -- consider splitting.
insufficient-modularization.remediation: Move cohesive play groups into roles or imported playbooks with explicit interfaces.

invalid-depends-on-reference.remediation: Replace the trailer value with a valid review URL or Gerrit Change-Id.

invalid-numeric-value.description: A numeric task/module value is outside its valid range.
invalid-numeric-value.remediation: Replace the literal with a value inside the reported valid range or validate a templated value before use.

invalid-task-attribute-type.description: A common Ansible task attribute has the wrong YAML type.
invalid-task-attribute-type.remediation: Use the YAML type required by the reported task attribute rather than a quoted or structurally incompatible value.

large-play.remediation: Split the play into cohesive task files or roles if doing so improves ownership and reuse.

large-playbook.remediation: Split independent responsibilities into roles or imported playbooks after confirming the threshold is appropriate.

large-task.remediation: Replace a monolithic task with a native module or smaller named tasks where semantics permit.

long-statement.description: A YAML source line exceeds the configured length threshold.
long-statement.remediation: Wrap or restructure the YAML/Jinja expression when possible; suppress only unavoidable generated values or URLs.

long-task-name.description: A task name exceeds the length threshold.
long-task-name.remediation: Shorten the name while preserving the operational intent developers need in Ansible output.

loop-legacy-syntax.description: A task uses deprecated with_* loop syntax; use loop: instead.
loop-legacy-syntax.remediation: Replace with_* loops with the unified loop: keyword introduced in Ansible 2.5 and use the corresponding Jinja2 filter or lookup.

missing-abstraction.description: A large task collection is not split into roles or included task files.
missing-abstraction.remediation: Split the large task collection along cohesive responsibilities when that improves navigation and reuse.

missing-bool-filters.description: A when: condition compares against a quoted boolean string.
missing-bool-filters.remediation: Convert the value explicitly with | bool or use a native boolean expression.

missing-bug-reference.description: A bug-fix commit message has no bug reference.
missing-bug-reference.remediation: Add the project-standard bug/issue reference to the relevant commit message.

missing-file-extension.description: A file reference is missing a file extension.
missing-file-extension.remediation: Use the complete referenced filename, including .yml/.yaml or the actual resource suffix.

missing-handler.description: A notify references a handler that does not exist.
missing-handler.remediation: Define the notified handler or correct the notify/listen name so repository-wide resolution succeeds.

missing-release-note.description: The latest configuration change has no release note.
missing-release-note.remediation: Add the project-standard release-note fragment or configure/document why this change is exempt.

missing-tags.description: Optional style policy: a task has no explicit or inherited tags.
missing-tags.remediation: Add an explicit or inherited tag only if the project needs selective execution; otherwise disable this optional rule.

missing-test-update.description: Configuration changed without a corresponding test change.
missing-test-update.remediation: Add or update a test/Molecule scenario that exercises the changed production behavior.

missing-validate-certs.description: TLS certificate validation is disabled on an HTTPS module (uri/get_url).
missing-validate-certs.remediation: Enable certificate validation and configure the trusted CA; document and narrowly suppress only justified bootstrap exceptions.

molecule-test-absent.description: Optional testing policy: an Ansible role has no Molecule test scenario.
molecule-test-absent.remediation: Create a molecule/ directory with at least one scenario to verify role behavior in an isolated environment.

non-idempotent-command.description: A mutating command lacks an idempotency guard.
non-idempotent-command.remediation: Use a native module or add creates/removes/changed_when/check_mode evidence that models the real state change.

overriden-keys.description: A duplicate mapping key silently discards a value.
overriden-keys.remediation: Keep one mapping entry for the key and merge the intended values explicitly.

overriding-facts.description: A set_fact variable is reassigned with a different value.
overriding-facts.remediation: Use one authoritative assignment or rename facts whose values represent different states.

plaintext-sensitive-variable.description: A sensitive variable is stored as a plaintext literal.
plaintext-sensitive-variable.remediation: Encrypt the value with Ansible Vault or replace it with a lookup from an approved secret manager.

read-only-command-change.description: A read-only command may report a change on every run.
read-only-command-change.remediation: Add changed_when: false to the read-only command or use a read-only Ansible information module.

redirected-module.description: A legacy module name should use its current collection FQCN.
redirected-module.remediation: Use the reported current collection FQCN to make resolution explicit.

redundant-default-value.description: An assignment repeats a value already supplied by role defaults.
redundant-default-value.remediation: Remove the identical override and rely on the role default unless the repetition is intentional policy documentation.

removed-copyright-notice.description: A copyright notice was removed by the latest commit.
removed-copyright-notice.remediation: Restore the notice unless its removal is intentional and legally reviewed.

role-readme-absent.description: Optional documentation policy: an Ansible role has no README.md file.
role-readme-absent.remediation: Add a README.md at the role root documenting inputs, outputs, and example usage.

role-variable-precedence-collision.description: A role variable is defined in both defaults and vars.
role-variable-precedence-collision.remediation: Keep overrideable values in defaults and reserve vars for deliberately fixed internal values.

shell-environment-export.description: A shell export is used instead of Ansible's environment mapping.
shell-environment-export.remediation: Move environment values to the task/play environment mapping instead of a standalone shell export.

shell-instead-of-module.description: A shell/command task could be replaced by a native Ansible module.
shell-instead-of-module.remediation: Replace the recognized command with the suggested native Ansible module when its semantics match.

silent-error-suppression.description: A task suppresses failure without retaining its result.
silent-error-suppression.remediation: Handle the failure explicitly: register and inspect the result, add recovery, or remove blanket suppression.

undocumented-complex-task.description: A complex task lacks a nearby explanatory comment.
undocumented-complex-task.remediation: Add a nearby comment explaining the non-obvious reason, constraint, or ordering—not a restatement of syntax.

unexpected-task-location.description: An Ansible document or handler-only task is placed in the wrong role directory.
unexpected-task-location.remediation: Move executable content to tasks/handlers and data to defaults/vars/meta according to the role layout.

unguarded-variable.description: A Jinja variable lacks a visible definition or safety guard.
unguarded-variable.remediation: Define the variable in visible scope or use default()/d()/is defined when absence is valid.

unnamed-play.remediation: Add a concise, action-oriented name to the play.

unnamed-task.remediation: Add a concise task name that describes the intended state or action.

unnecessary-abstraction.description: A block: wraps exactly one task.
unnecessary-abstraction.remediation: Remove the one-child block unless it intentionally supplies shared conditions, privilege, or error handling.

unnecessary-set-fact.description: A set_fact variable is never used.
unnecessary-set-fact.remediation: Remove the unused fact or reference it through a visible, documented data flow.

unpinned-ansible-dependency.description: An Ansible role or collection dependency has no fixed version.
unpinned-ansible-dependency.remediation: Pin the external role/collection to an immutable version or reviewed commit according to project policy.

unsafe-file-write.description: A file operation disables Ansible's atomic-write protection.
unsafe-file-write.remediation: Remove unsafe_writes: true unless the target filesystem cannot support atomic replacement; document the exception.

unscoped-shell-variable.description: A shell variable is not declared in Ansible's environment mapping.
unscoped-shell-variable.remediation: Declare the variable through environment, an inline assignment, or an explicit Ansible variable expansion.

unstructured-module.description: An Ansible role does not follow the conventional directory layout.
unstructured-module.remediation: Add the conventional role entry point or document/configure the intentional custom layout.

untested-override-change.description: Defaults or variables changed without an override test change.
untested-override-change.remediation: Add an override-focused test that supplies the changed option and asserts the resulting behavior.

unused-handler.description: A handler is defined but never notified.
unused-handler.remediation: Remove the handler or add the intended notify edge from the task that changes its resource.

unused-include-vars.description: An include_vars file's variables are never used.
unused-include-vars.remediation: Remove unused included variables or make their intended references explicit.

unused-registered-variable.description: A registered task result is never referenced.
unused-registered-variable.remediation: Remove register or inspect the result in a later condition, assertion, recovery, or diagnostic task.

variable-naming-convention.description: Optional naming policy: a role variable is not prefixed with the role name.
variable-naming-convention.remediation: Prefix role variables with the role name (e.g. myrole_varname) to avoid cross-role collisions.

variable-use-before-definition.description: A task uses a registered result or fact before a later task defines it.
variable-use-before-definition.remediation: Move the defining register/set_fact earlier or restructure the task order and guards.

vault-inline-overload.description: Optional organization policy: a role has many inline !vault | values.
vault-inline-overload.remediation: Move inline vault values to a dedicated vars/vault.yml or defaults/vault.yml and load it with include_vars.

yaml-formatting.description: A YAML formatting issue (indentation, trailing spaces, line endings).
yaml-formatting.remediation: Fix YAML formatting issues; use a linter or autoformatter with the project's configured style.

yaml-truthy-value.description: A YAML value uses 'yes'/'no' instead of the canonical 'true'/'false'.
yaml-truthy-value.remediation: Replace 'yes'/'no' with 'true'/'false' for YAML 1.2 compatibility and explicit intent.
